walkthroughs.body_html:
Brain and Neuropsychology — a core area of GCSE Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Brain and Neuropsychology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Brain and Neuropsychology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The brain and spinal cord together form the:
options: PNS
CNS
ANS
Somatic system

mcqs.q: Fight-or-flight is triggered by which nervous system branch?
options: Parasympathetic
Sympathetic
Somatic
Central

mcqs.q: Asch's line study primarily demonstrates which type of conformity?
options: Only through religious experience.
Informational social influence (believing others know better).
Normative social influence (compliance to fit in).
Internalisation of group beliefs.

mcqs.q: According to Maslow, when can self-actualisation be achieved?
options: Only after lower deficiency needs are largely met.
Only through religious experience.
Internalisation of group beliefs.
Anyone can self-actualise at any time through willpower.

mcqs.q: What are the three elements of Beck's negative triad?
options: Anger, sadness, and guilt.
Only through religious experience.
Negative views of past, present, and future.
Negative views of self, world, and future.
